home.title: Report street problems in Prishtina | kosova.report
home.description: A pothole, a dead street light, bins overflowing? Report it with a photo and the exact spot, and it goes to the department that handles it.

report.title: Report a problem in Prishtina | kosova.report
report.description: Pick a category, drop a pin, add photos. Your report gets a number, a private key and a PDF receipt. You can report without your name.

track.title: Find your report | kosova.report
track.description: Check your report's progress with the report number and the private key you got after sending it.

news.title: News from kosova.report | Updates and reports

cookies.title: Essential cookies only
cookies.intro: No ads and no analytics. We only use what the site needs to work.
cookies.essentialBody: Staff sign-in uses a security cookie. Your language and this notice are remembered on your device.
cookies.mapBody: Map tiles load from the map provider, which sees your IP address. It sets no cookies.
cookies.offlineBody: The app keeps only the offline page and icons on your device. Private reports are never cached. Your draft stays on this device until you send or delete it.
cookies.analyticsBody: Not used. There is nothing to switch on.

install.title: Keep kosova.report on your home screen
install.body: Open it like an app and report straight from the street, without looking for the site.
iosSteps: Tap the Share button at the bottom of the screen.
install.otherHelp: In other browsers, look for Install app in the browser menu.

how.title: One report, four parts
how.sub: Yes, it takes about two minutes. Most of that is finding the right spot on the map.

steps.title: Pick a category
steps.body: Seven areas, from roads to schools. The category decides which department receives the report.

steps.title: Drop the pin
steps.body: With your phone's location or one tap on the map. An exact spot saves a lot of questions later.

steps.title: Describe it, add a photo
steps.body: What's broken, since when, whether it's dangerous. A good photo says more than a paragraph.

steps.title: Send it and keep the proof
steps.body: You get a report number, a private key and a PDF receipt. Use them to follow the report later.

choice.title: With your name or without. Your call.
choice.anonymousBody: The department gets no contact details. You keep a private key and use it to check progress. Without the key, not even we can connect the report to you.
choice.namedBody: The department sees your email and can ask you for more detail. When the status changes, you get an email.
choice.keyCaption: Your private key. Only you have it.

home.categoriesSub: Pick an area and the report opens with it already chosen.

after.title: What happens after you send it

steps.title: The report goes to the department
steps.body: To the office that covers that category in your municipality, with the photos, the pin and your description.

steps.title: You have proof
steps.body: The report number, private key and PDF show that the report was sent, and when.

steps.title: The department updates the status
steps.body: When they mark it “Being handled” or “Resolved”, you see it with your key. If you left an email, you get a notice.

after.limits: This platform is not an emergency service. Submitting a report does not guarantee an immediate resolution. The department decides how and when to handle it.
after.emergency: If someone is in danger, call

together.title: Already reported? Add your voice.
together.sub: When many people report the same problem, it counts more. Before you send, you see what was already reported nearby.

items.title: One problem, one issue
items.body: Reports of the same pothole or rubbish pile are grouped into one public issue. The department sees how many people reported it.

items.title: I see it too
items.body: Give an issue a thumbs-up instead of sending the same report again. It takes one tap and needs no name.

items.title: Updates from the street
items.body: Add a comment or a photo when something changes, like “the road is blocked now”. Our team checks comments before they appear.

privacy.title: Privacy and cookies
privacy.intro: This page says exactly what happens to your data when you use kosova.report. We wrote it from what the platform actually does, not from a template.

sections.title: What we store when you report
body: When you send a report we store the category, the municipality, the coordinates of the pin, your description, the photos and the time it was sent. The report gets a number and a private key.
list: Photos are made smaller on your phone before sending, and the location, device and time details that cameras add automatically are removed.
Your email is stored only if you choose “With my email”. If you choose “Without my name”, we store no contact details at all.
The private key is the only way to see the report later without an email. Don't share it.

sections.title: Who sees your report
body: The report is emailed to the department that covers that category in your municipality: the description, the place on the map, the photos and, if you gave it, your email. The department gets a private link to mark the report “being handled” or “resolved”. That link expires after 90 days.
kosova.report staff who check reports see them in the staff panel. Your description, photos and email are never published automatically.

sections.title: Public issues, thumbs-up and comments
body: Each report belongs to a public issue, so people can see that a problem was already reported instead of sending it again. Several reports of the same problem are grouped into one issue: you choose this when you report, and staff can group or separate reports later.
list: Until staff check it, an issue page shows only the category, the approximate area (not the exact spot), the dates, the status and how many times it was reported.
Staff can then publish a summary they write themselves, the exact place and photos they choose. They leave out names, faces, plates and other personal details.
Your name, email, report number and private key are never shown on an issue page.
Reports sent before public issues existed stay private unless staff publish them.
A thumbs-up is counted once per browser. We store a scrambled code from a cookie, not your name or IP address.
Comments and their photos appear only after staff approve them. The name you type is shown with the comment; leave it empty to stay anonymous.

sections.title: Where the data is kept
list: Reports are stored in the database on the platform's server.

Photos are stored in Cloudflare R2, a file storage service. They are not public; only authorised staff see them, and the department through the email. A photo appears on an issue page only if staff choose it, or if it was attached to an approved comment.
Emails are sent through SMTP2Go, an email delivery service.

sections.title: Cookies and what stays on your device
body: We use no advertising or analytics cookies. There is nothing to switch on and nothing to refuse.
list: kr-locale: a cookie that remembers your language, for one year.
kr-voter: a random code, set only when you give a thumbs-up, so the same browser counts once. One year.
Staff sign-in cookie: only for staff who sign in to the staff panel.
Your browser storage keeps your choice for this notice and your theme (light, dark, high contrast).
A report draft, photos included, stays on this device only, until you send or delete it.
The report number and key are kept in this browser tab and disappear when you close it.

sections.title: The map and outside services
body: Map tiles load from the map provider (OpenStreetMap, unless another provider is set up). The provider sees your IP address, like any site you open. Fonts and the rest of the page load from our own server, with no outside services.

sections.title: Questions and requests
body: For questions about your data, or to ask for a report to be deleted, write to us and include the report number.
